Sign in to the [Amazon Lex console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/lex/home), and choose the bot that you want to edit.\\\\n2. Choose **Settings**, and then choose **Conversation logs**.\\\\n3. This feature allows granting principals in one account permission to call memory data plane APIs against resources in another account using resource-based policies. Memory delivery destinations, such as Amazon S3, Amazon SNS, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, can also be configured in a different account. Cross-account access is established by attaching a resource-policy to a memory resource, and principals in the consuming account can then create events, write memory records, retrieve records, and perform semantic search using the full memory ARN. Cross-account delivery destinations enable memory resources to deliver payloads and stream events to designated S3 buckets, SNS topics, and Kinesis Data Streams in other accounts. The documentation provides instructions on how to get started with cross-account memory access in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide. Also discovers which registration type a country requires from live API definitions and runs the universal registration lifecycle (create, derive fields, fill, submit, recover from denial, resubmit) shared by 10DLC, toll-free, short code, sender ID, RCS country launch, and Notify tier upgrade. If\\nthere is a policy already associated with a resource, you can use\\nthe console to view and modify the policy.\\n\\nWhen you save a policy with the policy editor, the console checks\\nthe syntax of the policy. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the Amazon Lex console at\\n   <https://console.aws.amazon.com/lex/>.\\n2. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the Amazon Lex console at\\n   <https://console.aws.amazon.com/lex/>.\\n2. From the **Bots** list, choose the bot\\n   that contains the alias that you want to edit.\\n3. From the left menu, choose **Aliases**,\\n   then choose the alias to edit.\\n4. In the **Resource-based policy** section,\\n   choose **Edit**.\\n\\n## Use the API to specify a resource-based policy\\n\\nYou can use API operations to manage the resource-based policies\\nfor your bots and bot aliases. There are operations to create,\\nupdate and delete policies.\\n\\nCreateResourcePolicy\\n:   Adds a new resource policy with the specified policy\\n    statements to a bot or bot alias.\\n\\nCreateResourcePolicyStatement\\n:   Adds a new resource policy statement to a bot or bot\\n    alias.\\n\\nDeleteResourcePolicy\\n:   Removes a resource policy from a bot or bot\\n    alias.\\n\\nDeleteResourcePolicyStatement\\n:   Removes a resource policy statement from a bot or bot\\n    alias.\\n\\nDescribeResourcePolicy\\n:   Gets a resource policy and the policy invoke lex:UpdateBotAlias on it.\\n         * The created policy will have revision id 1.\\n         */\\n\\n        CreateResourcePolicyRequest createPolicyRequest =\\n                CreateResourcePolicyRequest.builder()\\n                        .resourceArn(\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\")\\n                        .policy(\\\"{\\\\\\\"Version\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"2012-10-17\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Statement\\\\\\\": [{\\\\\\\"Sid\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"BotAliasEditor\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Effect\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Allow\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Principal\\\\\\\": {\\\\\\\"AWS\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"[redacted ARN]\\\\\\\"},\\\\\\\"Action\\\\\\\": [\\\\\\\"lex:UpdateBotAlias\\\\\\\"],\\\\\\\"Resource\\\\\\\":[\\\\\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\\\\\"]]}\\\")\\n\\n        lexmodelsv2Client.createResourcePolicy(createPolicyRequest);\\n\\n        /*\\n         * Overwrite the policy for the specified bot alias with a new policy.\\n         * Since no expectedRevisionId =\\n        UpdateResourcePolicyRequest.builder()\\n                        .resourceArn(\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\")\\n                        .policy(\\\"{\\\\\\\"Version\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"2012-10-17\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Statement\\\\\\\": [{\\\\\\\"Sid\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"BotAliasEditor\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Effect\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"Deny\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"Principal\\\\\\\": {\\\\\\\"AWS\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"[redacted ARN]\\\\\\\"},\\\\\\\"Action\\\\\\\": [\\\\\\\"lex:UpdateBotAlias\\\\\\\"],\\\\\\\"Resource\\\\\\\":[\\\\\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\\\\\"]]}\\\")\\n\\n        lexmodelsv2Client.updateResourcePolicy(updatePolicyRequest);\\n\\n        /*\\n         * Creates a statement in an existing policy for the specified bot alias\\n         * that allows a role to invoke lex:RecognizeText on it.\\n         * This request expects to update revision 2 of the policy. The request will fail\\n         * if the current revision of the policy is no longer revision 2.\\n         * After this request, the revision id for this policy will be 3.\\n         */\\n\\n deleteStatementRequest =\\n                DeleteResourcePolicyRequest.builder()\\n                        .resourceArn(\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\")\\n Describe the current policy for the specified bot alias\\n         * It always returns the current revision.\\n         */\\n        DescribeResourcePolicyRequest describePolicyRequest =\\n                DescribeResourcePolicyRequest.builder()\\n                        .resourceArn(\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\")\\n                        .build();\\n\\n        lexmodelsv2Client.describeResourcePolicy(describePolicyRequest);\\n\\n        /*\\n         * Delete the current policy for the specified bot alias\\n         * This request expects to delete revision 3 of the policy. Since the revision id for\\n         * this policy is already at 4, this request will fail.\\n         */\\n        DeleteResourcePolicyRequest deletePolicyRequest =\\n                DeleteResourcePolicyRequest.builder()\\n                        .resourceArn(\\\"arn:aws:lex:Region:123456789012:bot-alias/MYBOTALIAS/TSTALIASID\\\")\\n                        .expectedRevisionId(3);\\n                        .build();\\n\\n        lexmodelsv2Client.deleteResourcePolicy(deletePolicyRequest);\\n```\\n\\n## Allow an IAM role to update a bot and list bot aliases\\n\\nThe following example grants permissions for a specific IAM\\nrole to call Amazon Lex V2 model building API operations to modify an\\nexisting bot.
